The guide does not address condos or townhomes (searched condo, townhome, townhouse, unit owner; only 'boat slip condos' appears, as non-standard construction).
Asphalt shingle, light metal panel, built-up (with or without gravel) and single-ply membrane (including ballasted) roofs under 15 years old are settled at replacement cost (RCV).
Asphalt shingle, light metal panel, built-up (with or without gravel) and single-ply membrane (including ballasted) roofs 15-25 years old are limited to actual cash value (ACV).
Asphalt shingle, light metal panel, built-up (with or without gravel) and single-ply membrane (including ballasted) roofs over 25 years old have roof coverage excluded.
Hurricane-rated shingle and wooden shingle roofs under 20 years old are settled at replacement cost (RCV).
Hurricane-rated shingle and wooden shingle roofs 20-25 years old are limited to actual cash value (ACV).
Standing seam metal, clay/concrete tile and slate roofs under 35 years old are settled at replacement cost (RCV).
Standing seam metal, clay/concrete tile and slate roofs 35-40 years old are limited to actual cash value (ACV).
Underwriting may change roof loss settlement for any risk based on inspection, loss history or other factors, regardless of roof age or material.
Soft story construction is ineligible for the optional earthquake endorsement.
Unreinforced masonry construction is ineligible for the optional earthquake endorsement.
A $300,000 pool liability sublimit applies when Coverage E is $300,000 or more.
Homes with a prior animal bite claim are ineligible.
Liability is excluded for animals bred or kept for commercial purposes.
The guide does not address solar panels (searched solar, photovoltaic, PV, panel; 'panel' appears only for roofs and breaker panels).
Protection classes 1 through 10 are eligible.
Coverage B is 0-20% of Coverage A.
Coverage C is 0-80% of Coverage A, with a personal property replacement cost option.
Coverage D is 0-30% of Coverage A.
Open claims with prior carriers make the home ineligible.
One water damage loss under $25,000 in the last 3 years brings a water damage exclusion.
A prior animal bite claim makes the home ineligible.
Optional identity fraud coverage of $15,000 with a $500 deductible is available.
Homes more than 5 miles from an ISO-rated responding fire department are ineligible.
Applicant must hold title to the home, with no more than 2 mortgages.
Residence must be owner-occupied by the owner's immediate family.
Metal roofs must carry the Non-Structural Hail Loss Limitation Endorsement.
Roofs 15 years or older are covered on an Actual Cash Value basis.
On HOA-Plus, roof coverings 15 years or older are settled at Actual Cash Value.
Protection class 10 (more than 5 miles from a fire station, in split-class areas) is ineligible.
In split-class areas, homes within 5 miles of a fire station and more than 1,000 ft from a hydrant are class 9; within 1,000 ft get the first class.
Homes more than 5 miles from an ISO-rated responding fire department are ineligible.
Applicant must hold title to the home, with no more than 2 mortgages.
Residence must be occupied by the owner and the owner's immediate family.
Home must be in very good condition, and wiring, plumbing, heating and roof must meet the guide's requirements.
Plumbing fixtures and the water heater tank must meet code.
Normal roof wear and granule loss are acceptable.
Metal roofs must carry the Non-Structural Hail Loss Limitation Endorsement.
Roofs 15 years or older are covered on an Actual Cash Value basis.
Kerosene, coal, wood or solar as a heating fuel source is unacceptable (Heating and Cooling section; does not address solar panels).
Guide does not address solar panels; solar is only mentioned as an unacceptable heating fuel (see ARB-062).

In First and Second Tier Counties (territories 01X, 08X, 09X, 10X, 11X), agent binding authority for new business and coverage increases ends when a hurricane or tropical storm watch/warning is issued for, or a storm enters, the Gulf of Mexico (or is west of 80 W and north of 20 N).
Single Building definition: buildings separated by space, or by a 6 inch reinforced concrete or 8 inch masonry party wall to the roof and exterior walls, are separate buildings.
Homes more than 5 miles from a fire station are Protection Class 10 and ineligible.
In split-class areas, homes less than 5 miles from a fire station and more than 1,000 ft from a hydrant are Protection Class 9.
During a Company emergency restriction, new risks may not be bound and existing policies may not increase limits, lower deductibles or add coverages.
Foremost Choice Homeowners Other Structures limits above 40% of Coverage A exceed producer binding authority and need Underwriting Approval.
Dwellings attached to a commercial building are ineligible unless they share only a side firewall and are deeded separately.
The year roof updated is entered only when the entire roof covering has been replaced.
Foremost Choice Homeowners settles partial losses to roofs 15 years old or older at actual cash value.
Solar shingles make the dwelling ineligible.
Dwellings with neighboring structures that are abandoned, have unrepaired damage or otherwise increase the likelihood of loss are ineligible.
Foremost Choice Homeowners must carry the 2% Wind & Hail deductible in all territories except W, Y and Z when an All Other Peril deductible under 2% is chosen.
Foremost Choice Homeowners carries a mandatory 2% Tropical Cyclone deductible in Territories W and Y.
Owner-occupied dwellings with more than 3 owners who are not members of the same primary household are ineligible.

For owner-occupied policies, a Governmental Entity, Land Trust, Conservatorship, Co-op, Condominium Association or business (including a corporation or lending institution) may not be the Named Insured.
For owner-occupied risks, an LLC is the only eligible business name, and only if no business is associated with the name.
For owner-occupied homes in a family or living trust, the person living in the home must be the grantor and/or the trustee.
For owner-occupied homes held as a life estate, the Life Tenant must live in the dwelling.
On renewal, any occupied residence may have at most 5 paid losses.
A fire, water plumbing, water appliance or accidental discharge loss of $500 or more, combined with 1 or more other loss of $500 or more, all at the insuring location, is ineligible.
Water Backup of Sewers or Drains coverage needs Underwriting Approval if the applicant had 2 or more backup, flood, water plumbing, water weather, water appliance or accidental discharge/leak losses.

Farm/ranch exposure qualifies as incidental only if the applicant earns $5,000 or less per year from farming, farms less than 26 acres, has no full/part-time workers, no u-pick, no land rented/leased/made available to others, and no farm animals (excluding poultry) kept in an unfenced area, boarded or bred for others, more than 10 owned, or used for riding lessons/rentals.
Foremost Choice Homeowners dwellings and other structures must be free of physical defects to siding, roof, chimney, porch and foundation, with no signs of deterioration or existing damage.
Properties with business activities are unacceptable for liability, unless the home is primary owner-occupied and the business is incidental, in which case refer to Underwriting Approval.

Incidental business on a primary owner-occupied home is subject to Underwriting Approval and must not add significant traffic, have advertising signs, use hazardous materials or have employees on premises.
Properties with business activities, including incidental business on a primary owner-occupied home, require Underwriting Approval.
Multiple dwellings on the same premises with common grounds (clubhouse, playground, beach, pool, pond, bathhouse, laundry, rental office or parking lot) are unacceptable for liability.
PPC 8-10 (including 10W) is eligible only on homes 3 years old or newer; PPC 8-10 homes older than 3 years are ineligible (all forms).
On homes 3 years old or newer with PPC 8-10 (10W), underwriting review and approval is required before binding (all forms).
Trampolines have no liability coverage on HO3 (and HOB, HOA with Replacement Cost); the home stays eligible.
Prohibited animals have no liability coverage on HO3 (and HOB, HOA with Replacement Cost); the home stays eligible.
Acceptable animals have a $25,000 liability limit on HO3 (and HOB, HOA with Replacement Cost) unless Full Animal Liability is added.
On HO3 (and HOB), foundation damage from plumbing/heating/AC water is covered up to 15% of Coverage A capped at $25,000, and $10,000 on homes over 35 years old.
On HO3 (and HOB), sudden and accidental plumbing/heating/AC water discharge is covered, and on homes over 20 years old only by endorsement.
On HO3, continuous or repeated leakage from plumbing/heating/AC is covered only by endorsement.
On HO3 (and HOB), Solar Panel Coverage is available by endorsement.
The dwelling must be occupied, unless it is an eligible building in the course of construction.
The dwelling must be used for private residential purposes, apart from permitted incidental business occupancies.

When a 2-4 unit dwelling is occupied by joint owners in separate units, the policy is issued to only one joint owner/occupant (it may be endorsed to cover the other joint owners' interests and premises liability).
If the premises is used for farming, the farming must be incidental to the dwelling occupancy and not the insured's occupation.
If the premises is used for business, it must be a permitted business occupancy, incidental to a dwelling occupied principally as a private residence.
Tenant (renters) policies need Coverage C of at least $5,000.

Buildings in the course of construction or extensive renovation are acceptable only if completed and occupied within 12 months, done by a licensed, bonded, insured contractor who is not the named insured, carry the Theft of Building Materials Endorsement if vacant, and have Coverage A of $1 million or less.
The roof must be within functional life and in good condition, except for eligible buildings in the course of construction.
Non-standard buildings are ineligible; barndominiums (metal structures with metal roofs) are allowed if on a concrete foundation with no aluminum siding or existing damage.
For a vacant building under construction or extensive renovation, the Theft of Building Materials Endorsement must be carried.
For a building under construction or extensive renovation, Coverage A over $1 million is ineligible.

Unoccupied buildings (furnished but not used as a residence, e.g. unoccupied 30+ consecutive days 4+ times a year) are ineligible, except eligible buildings under construction; seasonal or secondary homes are not considered unoccupied.

Vacant buildings (lacking amenities, furnishings or utilities for normal occupancy) are ineligible, except eligible buildings under construction; a dwelling under construction or renovation is not considered vacant.
In Protection Class 9, homes with Coverage A over $3 million are ineligible.
In Protection Class 10, homes with Coverage A over $1 million are ineligible.
A single non-weather water loss alone is not a reason to reject, cancel or non-renew.
Fewer than 3 remediated appliance-related water losses alone are not a reason to reject, cancel or non-renew.
In Protection Class 9, homes with Coverage A of $1.5 million or more must be referred to underwriting.
All Protection Class 10 homes must be referred to underwriting.
For Protection Class 9 homes with Coverage A $1.5-3 million and all Protection Class 10 homes, the dwelling must be within 15 miles of a responding fire department.
For Protection Class 9 homes with Coverage A $1.5-3 million and all Protection Class 10 homes, a wood or coal burning stove cannot be the primary heat source.

For Protection Class 9 homes with Coverage A $1.5-3 million and all Protection Class 10 homes, there must be a smoke or heat alarm on every floor and fire extinguishers or a Central Station Fire Alarm.
For Protection Class 9 homes with Coverage A $1.5-3 million and all Protection Class 10 homes, there must be a local water source.
For Protection Class 9 homes with Coverage A $1.5-3 million and all Protection Class 10 homes, the property must be accessible year-round.
Townhomes, row homes and multi-unit residences must have a fire wall between units extending to the roof line.
A crawl space must be fully enclosed on all sides with permanent material (block, brick, siding, etc.).
Homes with renewable energy systems (including solar panels) are eligible.
Renewable energy systems (solar panels, wind turbines, geothermal heat pumps, micro hydropower, rainwater catchment) are excluded from coverage.
Protection class 10 is ineligible.
Any wear and tear, damage or deterioration that could increase the potential for loss is ineligible.
Damaged, missing or deteriorating siding is ineligible.
Damaged, deteriorating, dilapidated or dangerous detached structures (garages, sheds, barns, fences, pools, trampolines, tree houses, skate ramps) are ineligible.
Cracked, crumbling or damaged foundations are ineligible.
Excessive yard debris (wood piles, brush, materials, inoperable vehicles) is ineligible.

In split-class areas, homes more than 5 miles from a fire station are PC 10 (ineligible); within 5 miles but more than 1,000 ft from a hydrant they are PC 9; within 5 miles and 1,000 ft they take the first PC.
The Weather/Wildfire deductible cannot be less than the Non-Weather deductible.
Weather/Wildfire deductible options are 2%, 3%, 5%, 10%, $25,000, $50,000 or $100,000.
Homes 30+ years old, or with cast iron, galvanized, pre-2006 PEX or polybutylene plumbing, or a tank water heater above the ground floor, get a $10,000 non-weather water damage limit.
The named insured's credit-based insurance score is used for eligibility, but no threshold is stated.
Homes must be 100 years old or newer (by year of construction); completely renovated homes may use the renovation year as the construction year.

The guide rates these construction types: aluminum siding, fire resistive, frame, frame with Hardiplank siding, log, masonry, brick/stone/masonry veneer and vinyl siding. It does not say other types are ineligible, so confirm any unlisted type (e.g. true stucco) with underwriting.
Animal liability has a $100,000 annual sublimit under Coverage E.
Seasonal or secondary homes are ineligible unless owner occupied and at least 50 miles from the primary residence.
Tesla Solar Roofs and solar roofs, including Tesla batteries or any Tesla parts, are ineligible.
Any prior sinkhole activity or sinkhole claim is ineligible.
Animal liability (Coverage E) has an annual sublimit of $50,000.
On homes older than 40 years with 1 water loss under $25K, a $2,000 minimum deductible is required.
Homes left unoccupied more than 10 days without the plumbing turned off are subject to the Escape of Water Exclusion.
Light metal panel roofs settle at RCV under 15 years, ACV at 15-25 years, and roof coverage is excluded over 25 years.
Seasonal or secondary homes whose owner's primary residence is outside the United States are ineligible.
ISO protection class 9 or 10 is ineligible.
Prior sinkhole activity or sinkhole claims are ineligible.
Coverage B is up to 40% of Coverage A, Coverage C up to 50%, Coverage D up to 20% (B and D subject to minimums).

Listed construction types are aluminum siding, fire resistive, frame, frame with Hardiplank siding, log, masonry, brick/stone/masonry veneer and vinyl siding; the guide does not say whether other types are ineligible.
Animal liability is sublimited to $100,000 annually under Coverage E.
Homes that are vacant, unoccupied, under construction, for sale or used for non-habitational purposes are ineligible.
Any prior sinkhole activity or sinkhole claim makes the risk ineligible.
The home must be occupied by the owner or the owner's immediate family.

Homes of unconventional construction (log, do-it-yourself, dome, shell, unconventional parts, or not meeting building codes) are ineligible. Solar panels are handled in TWI-033 (agency decision: standard code-compliant mounted panels are eligible).

Solar panels are listed as unconventional construction (ineligible); by agency decision of 2026-10-06, standard code-compliant mounted solar panels are treated as eligible, so only non-standard or non-code-compliant solar installations decline.
Wood, asbestos, slate, aluminum shake, metal tile/shake/shingle and corrugated metal roofs are ineligible.
Homes where the fire department response time is more than 10 minutes are ineligible.
Composition 3-tab roofs are settled at replacement cost at age 0-10 years, ACV at age 11-20 years, and roof coverage is excluded at age 21+ years.
Architectural composition roofs are settled at replacement cost at age 0-15 years, ACV at age 16-25 years, and roof coverage is excluded at age 26+ years.
Standing-seam metal roofs are settled at replacement cost at age 0-20 years, ACV at age 21-35 years, and roof coverage is excluded at age 36+ years.
Concrete/clay tile roofs are settled at replacement cost at age 0-25 years, ACV at age 26-45 years, and roof coverage is excluded at age 46+ years.
Except on Tenant policies, more than 1 paid water damage claim in the past 3 years (by the applicant or at the risk location) is ineligible.

Except on Tenant policies, a mold claim in the past 3 years is ineligible unless a Certificate of Mold Damage Remediation (MDR-1) is provided; the risk cannot be bound until it is submitted to Underwriting.
Except on Tenant policies, 3 or more paid appliance-related claims in the past 3 years (by the applicant or at the risk location) is ineligible.
Unprotected ground-mounted solar panels are ineligible.

A dwelling, other structures, land or major systems (plumbing, heating, electrical, roof) not in good condition, with unrepaired/unmaintained conditions, or with uncorrected fire or building code violations is ineligible.
A tenant risk with Coverage C plus Additions and Alterations of $500,000 or more must have a monitored central station fire and burglar alarm system.
A risk more than 7 road miles from the first responding fire department is ineligible.
A vacant or unoccupied home is ineligible unless it will be occupied within 30 days of the effective date (e.g. newly purchased or under renovation).
In Wind/Hail/Tornado UW Classifications High 1 and High 2, a roof (other than tile, slate or similar lifetime material) not replaced within the past 10 years is ineligible.
In Wind/Hail/Tornado UW Classification High 3, a roof (other than tile, slate or similar lifetime material) not replaced within the past 15 years is ineligible.
In all other Wind/Hail/Tornado UW Classifications, a roof (other than tile, slate or similar lifetime material) not replaced within the past 25 years is ineligible.

An owner-occupied home with a wood, coal, pellet stove or other wood-burning device as alternate or supplemental heat is ineligible unless professionally installed or inspected and approved by the local fire department or building inspector.
A dwelling or condo used in whole or part for other than private residential purposes (e.g. bed & breakfast, hostel, boarding home, multi-roomer) is ineligible.
A condo held for rent that contains a wood, coal or pellet stove is ineligible.
A secondary or seasonal home with Coverage A of $500,000 or more without both a monitored central station fire and burglar alarm must be referred to underwriting.
A tenant risk with Coverage C plus Additions & Alterations of $500,000 or more must be approved by underwriting before binding.
Travelers may suspend binding for hurricanes, tropical storms, wildfires, earthquakes or other catastrophes until an announcement lifts it; current suspensions are posted on For Agents.
Dwellings in flood zones starting with V or A are ineligible unless covered by a flood policy up to the Coverage A limit or the FEMA maximum of $250,000, whichever is less.
Dwellings in Hurricane UW Classifications High 1 and High 2 require a flood policy up to the Coverage A limit or the FEMA maximum of $250,000, whichever is less.
For Condo, Landlord Condo and Tenant in Hurricane UW Classifications High 1/High 2, total Loss Assessment coverage cannot exceed $25K.
Dwelling risks with a Maximum FireLine score other than 0-30 must be referred to underwriting before binding.
The dwelling must be used solely for residential purposes; permitted incidental occupancies and up to 3 roomers or boarders are allowed.
Risks with a trampoline may be declined or cancelled at Underwriting's discretion.
Risks with a pool diving board and/or slide may be declined or cancelled at Underwriting's discretion.
Composition shingle roofs 16 years old or older must carry the ACV Windstorm or Hail Losses to Roof Surfacing endorsement.
Architectural shingle roofs 25 years old or older must carry the ACV Windstorm or Hail Losses to Roof Surfacing endorsement.
Protection class 9 or 10 is ineligible unless approved by Underwriting.
Dwellings with exotic, farm or saddle animals are ineligible.
Crawlspaces/enclosed piers up to 6 ft elevation are acceptable when enclosed with permanent materials such as block or brick siding, not lattice.
Open foundations/open piers up to 6 ft on homes built 1965 through 2005 are acceptable if Coverage A is $200,000 or more.
Open foundations/open piers up to 6 ft on homes built 1965 through 2005 with Coverage A under $200,000 must be referred to Underwriting with photos.
Single-family dwellings with Coverage A from $750,001 to $2,000,000 are eligible as high value homes; Coverage A above $2,000,000 is not provided for.
Claims are evaluated for rating and underwriting; Act of God claims alone cannot be the basis to non-renew, cancel or surcharge unless the insured failed to prevent recurrence.
An incidental occupancy must be operated by the insured owner or a resident relative of the owner.
Offices, schools or studios (business/professional offices; private music, dance, photography or other instruction) are permitted incidental occupancies.

A minimum 2% wind/hail deductible is required in Tier 2 counties (Hidalgo, Brooks, Jim Wells, Live Oak, Bee, Goliad, Victoria, Jackson, Wharton, Fort Bend, Harris outside the Windpool area, Liberty, Hardin, Orange) and other counties shown on Centauri's system; a lower deductible may be allowed with Underwriting approval.
The guide does not address solar panels.
An applicant who was a first party in a personal lawsuit against an auto or homeowners insurer is ineligible, unless the applicant prevailed in or settled the lawsuit.
A risk with a trampoline may be declined or cancelled at underwriting's discretion.
A risk with a pool slide or diving board may be declined or cancelled at underwriting's discretion.
A minimum 1% windstorm or hail deductible is required in all counties open for binding.
A minimum 2% hurricane deductible is required in all counties open for binding.
Flat, rock, tar, gravel, asbestos shingle, wood, rolled, sheet tin and aluminum (including galvanized) roofs are ineligible.
Metal, steel or aluminum roofs must be written with the Cosmetic Damage exclusion (ECD) for wind/hail.
Roofs may be inspected based on age and material; roofs not in acceptable condition may be declined or settled at ACV (form ACVR) as underwriting decides.
Homes 40 years and older are written with Limited Water Damage (LWD) at $10,000; higher up to the lesser of 10% of Cov A or $50,000; removal needs proof of plumbing upgrades and UW approval.
Flat, asbestos shingle, wood shake, rolled, sheet tin, aluminum (including galvanized), tar and gravel, and built-up roofs are ineligible.
Protection class 9 or 10 is ineligible.
Dwellings or detached structures showing poor maintenance, deferred maintenance, structural deterioration or conditions that increase loss potential are ineligible.
Wind deductible Zone A counties: Aransas, Brazoria, Calhoun, Cameron, Chambers, Galveston, Jefferson, Kenedy, Kleberg, Matagorda, Nueces, Refugio, San Patricio, Willacy, and Harris east of SH 146.

Wind deductible Zone B counties: Bee, Brooks, Fort Bend, Goliad, Hardin, Harris west of SH 146, Hidalgo, Jackson, Jim Wells, Liberty, Live Oak, Montgomery, Orange, Victoria, Wharton; Zone C is the rest of the state.
Scheduled property requests are denied when the named insured has any prior or outstanding vandalism, theft or mysterious disappearance claims.
In PPC 1-7, dwelling (Coverage A) limit is at most $500,000.
In PPC 8-10, dwelling (Coverage A) limit is at most $300,000; PPC 8-10 is otherwise listed as written.
Contents coverage is limited to 40% (of the dwelling limit).
Cosmetic hail loss payout is capped at 2% of the dwelling limit (mandatory Cosmetic Hail Loss Limitation endorsement).
Hail damage that is only dents, scratches or nicks to carports or exterior surfaces is limited (mandatory Non-Structural Hail Loss Limitation endorsement).
Wind and hail roof losses are paid on a roof systems payment schedule (percentage of cost) under a mandatory endorsement.
Seasonal dwellings and short-term rentals must be occupied by a tenant more often than by the owner.
Seasonal dwellings and short-term rentals may not be occupied by the owner for more than 5 consecutive months a year.
Every unit in the building must be occupied by tenants.

Owner-occupied dwellings are ineligible (includes an owner living in one unit of a multi-unit building, or a short-term/seasonal rental the owner occupies more than tenants or for more than 5 consecutive months a year).
A multi-unit dwelling where the owner lives in one unit counts as owner-occupied and is ineligible.
Buildings with more than 4 units, or units not designed for one-family occupancy, are ineligible.
The property must be well maintained, occupied and not unduly exposed to loss.
All major systems (plumbing, heating, electrical, roof) must be in good condition with no unreported conditions or uncorrected fire or building code violations.
If a wood or coal furnace or boiler is the primary heat source, the dwelling must have a backup oil or gas central heating or thermostatically controlled electric system.
Losses counted are all paid losses (including CAT) in the last 5 years to the dwelling or contents at this location while owned by the insured.
Guide does not address solar panels.
Guide does not address protection class, fire station distance or hydrants.
In protection class 1-8, the maximum dwelling (Coverage A) limit is $1,500,000.
In protection class 9 (including 1X-8X variations), the maximum dwelling (Coverage A) limit is $750,000.
In protection class 10 (all variations), the maximum dwelling (Coverage A) limit is $500,000.
In protection class 1-8, dwelling limits between $1,000,000 and $1,500,000 need underwriting approval.
Properties over $1,500,000 or over 5,000 square feet must carry the Extended Replacement Cost endorsement.
In protection class 1-8, a central station fire alarm is required when the amount of insurance is over $1,000,000.
In protection class 9 (including 1X-8X variations), a central station fire alarm is required when the amount of insurance is over $750,000.
In protection class 10 (all variations), a central station fire alarm is required when the amount of insurance is over $500,000.
When a central station fire alarm is required on a multi-family structure, each unit must have sensors connected to the central station.
Vandalism coverage does not apply if the dwelling was vacant or unoccupied more than 60 consecutive days before the loss.
For the Course of Construction endorsement, the minimum deductible is $1,500.

Dwellings built in 1940 or earlier can only be written at ACV unless roof, electrical panel, wiring, plumbing, heating and water heater were all renovated in the past 15 years (documentation to underwriting).
Under the Roof Payment Schedule, wind and hail roof losses are settled as a percentage of replacement cost based on roof age and material.
An animal is dangerous (ineligible) if the carrier has had a bite injury claim from it in the past 5 years.
An animal is dangerous (ineligible) if a medical report shows it caused injuries, with or without a claim.
In protection class 9-10, dwellings must be within 10 road miles of the first responding fire department.
In protection class 9-10, dwellings must have site access adequate for a fire truck to reach the structure.
In protection class 1-9, a Cotality Wildfire Risk Score of 61 or higher is ineligible.
In protection class 10, a Cotality Wildfire Risk Score of 41 or higher is ineligible.
With a wildfire score of 51-60, the dwelling must have no wood siding or open/exposed areas to pass the Brush Inspection.
With a wildfire score of 51-60, the property boundary must be free of construction materials, pine needles, leaves and other flammable debris to pass the Brush Inspection.
Property with unmitigated or unrepaired damage from a prior loss is ineligible.
Non-remediated mold, fire, vandalism, theft/burglary or flood losses in the last 5 years are ineligible.
Guide does not address solar panels.
Guide does not address lot size or acreage (only farming exposure, which is ineligible).
Seasonal or secondary dwellings are acceptable only on Dwelling forms, only if owner occupied and the primary dwelling is insured with National General.
Homes older than 40 years that have not had plumbing and wiring updates are ineligible; homes older than 40 years must be submitted before binding.
On homes over 40 years old, all kitchens and bathrooms must be completely renovated, including plumbing, cabinetry, appliances and floors.
On homes over 40 years old, kitchen and bathroom updates must be visible in photos and water heater age should be provided.
Asbestos, EIFS, wood shingle and asbestos shingle siding is ineligible.
Wood shingle, aluminum, EIFS and asbestos siding is not acceptable.
If liability coverage applies and a listed vicious breed is found at the home at inspection, the policy is cancelled permanently with no exceptions.
Applicants with exotic, saddle or farm animals are ineligible.
Homes with solar panels are ineligible.
Risks with unrepaired damage from a previous insurance claim are ineligible.
On TDP forms, personal property is not available on tenant-occupied dwellings; 0% to 70% of the dwelling limit is available on owner-occupied dwellings.
Seasonal/secondary owner-occupied homes occupied by the owner more than 4 months are permitted.
A dwelling occupied by the owner for less than 9 continuous months per year is considered secondary/seasonal.
Vacant, unoccupied, under-construction, or majorly renovating properties are ineligible.
Trees must be a safe distance from structures and trimmed; homes with trees overhanging the roof or dangerously close may be ineligible.
Applicant must hold title to the home, and the home may have no more than 2 mortgages.
For townhouses/rowhouses, Coverage A may be issued only when the dwelling has 4 or fewer family units within a Fire Division.
Owner-as-builder construction risks are ineligible.
Asbestos roof or siding is ineligible.
Homes over 40 years old get ACV loss settlement on Coverage A and B (DP 04 76), waivable for substantially renovated homes with Underwriting approval of proof of updates.
Properties with exotic, farm, saddle, or hooved animals are ineligible.
Liability coverage excludes damages caused by animals.
In split-class unclassified areas, under 5 miles and under 1,000 ft from a hydrant gets the first PC; under 5 miles and over 1,000 ft is PC 9; over 5 miles is PC 10.
A minimum wind/hail deductible of 2% of Coverage A is required, and it cannot be less than the All Other Perils deductible.
Units must be used only for private residential purposes.
Units with a home day care exposure are ineligible.
Units used as college housing are ineligible.
Units used for business purposes are ineligible.
Units that are vacant, unoccupied, under construction or undergoing major renovation are ineligible.
Units rented for periods of less than 1 year carry a short-term rental surcharge.
Units with any rental exposure must carry the Unit-Owners Rental to Others endorsement.
The applicant must hold title to the unit, and the unit may have no more than 2 mortgages.
In Protection Class 8 or higher, any fire loss makes the unit ineligible.
Units within 1/2 mile of the coast must be above FEMA base flood elevation.
In Protection Class 9 or 10, the unit must be on a paved road.
In Protection Class 9 or 10, the unit must be visible to neighbors.
Split classes are set by distance: under 5 miles to a station and over 1,000 feet to a hydrant is PC 9; over 5 miles is PC 10; unclassified areas are PC 10.
Units must have a professionally installed, permanent, thermostatically controlled central heat source.
Units using space heaters are ineligible.
Units must have a professionally installed, permanent, thermostatically controlled central cooling system.
Units bought through foreclosure or short sale need underwriting approval before binding, with a home inspection and photos.
Units in foreclosure are ineligible.
Units with settling or cracking of the foundation and/or walls are ineligible.
Trees or brush overhanging the roof or dangerously close to the dwelling or other structures make the risk ineligible.
On units more than 40 years old, removing the Limited Water Damage endorsement requires electrical, heating, plumbing and roof updates completed within the past 10 years.
